pins: protocol-survey.md §4 -- transaction layout, hashing and validation
rule: Every value below was returned by a function in reference/. Nothing here is hand-computed. Regenerate rather than edit.

identity.note: one WOTS+ identity used by every vector in this group, derived by the reference's own tx_bot_get_wots() from a fixed secret.
identity.adrs_tail12_source: types.h:442-443 -- "The last 12 bytes of the Address Scheme MUST contain the hexadecimal string 420000000e00000001000000"

txentry_layout.note: TXENTRY is the one struct in the group with alignment > 1 and the one types.h does not assert. Every off_* on a vector is measured from tx->buffer, so none of them pins these.

vectors.note: minimal single-destination transaction with a zero amount. SERIALIZATION ONLY -- mdst_val() rejects zero amounts (tx.c:606-609), so this is not a valid transaction. The fixture plan called D1 the minimal valid transaction; that was wrong, and D1v below is the correction.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: tx_sz = 116 + 44N + 2208 + 40, dsaoff = 116 + 44N
vectors.mdst_val_errno_text: eXtended TX destination amount is zero

vectors.note: the minimal VALID single-destination transaction: same shape as D1 with a non-zero amount, fully signed. Both validators reachable offline are run over it.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: a one-destination transaction with a non-zero amount and matching totals validates

vectors.note: two destinations with distinct tags and amounts. The first vector where a fixed-offset implementation puts the signature in the wrong place.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: the DSA block follows the destination array, so its offset moves with N

vectors.note: three destinations. Confirms the 44-byte stride rather than merely 'not one'.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: sizeof(MDST) = 44

vectors.note: 256 destinations -- the maximum the option byte can encode. Proves the TXENTRY buffer bound is exact: tx_sz here must equal sizeof(TXENTRY.buffer).
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: MDST_COUNT is zero-based, so 255 encodes 256 destinations

vectors.note: 255 destinations. Off-by-one guard beside D4.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: MDST_COUNT is zero-based

vectors.note: options[2] = 0. Pins the zero-based count: byte 0 means ONE destination. An implementation that writes the true count builds a transaction one destination too long, which serializes cleanly and fails validation.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: MDST_COUNT(options) = options[2] + 1

vectors.note: options[2] = 255, the other end of the same encoding.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: MDST_COUNT(options) = options[2] + 1

vectors.note: boundary 64-bit values written through put64(). One field is 0x0102030405060708 rather than all-0xff, because an all-0xff value is a palindrome and hides a byte-order error.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: 64-bit fields are little-endian on the wire

vectors.note: NEGATIVE -- adrs word 5 changed from 0x42 to 0x43. tx_val__wots requires the stored address scheme to equal the scheme wots_pk_from_sig leaves behind, AND requires its last 12 bytes to be exactly {0x42, 0x0e, 0x01}. Settles survey open question 8: the terminal value is checked, not merely produced.
vectors.falsifies: survey open question 8: the adrs terminal state is enforced by the validator

vectors.note: the source address TAG half corrupted AFTER signing, hash half left correct. The fixture plan predicted this would still pass, on the reading that tx_val__wots compares only ADDR_HASH_PTR against the recovered key. It does -- but src_addr sits inside TXHDR, which is inside the signed range, so altering the tag half changes the message hash, which changes the recovered public key, which changes its address hash. The prediction was wrong for a reason the reading missed. message_hash_changed below is the mechanism, and Ds8b isolates the validator's own behaviour from the signature's.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3(b): the address tag half is outside what the signature commits to

vectors.note: the source address tag half set to 20 x 0xa5 BEFORE signing, so the signature is valid for the transaction as written. Isolates the validator from the signature: tx_val__wots checks only ADDR_HASH_PTR (tx.c:688), so a tag half that is not the address hash is accepted here. Whether such an address is acceptable at all is decided by the ledger in tx_val(), which is not callable offline.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3(b): tx_val__wots does not constrain the address tag half

vectors.note: the source address HASH half corrupted. The positive control for Ds8: this must fail.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3(b): the WOTS+ signature binds the address hash half

vectors.note: NEGATIVE -- one bit flipped in the signature. The control that proves Ds6 is not passing vacuously.
vectors.falsifies: survey §3: recovery is sensitive to every signature byte

vectors.note: NEGATIVE -- the destination amount altered after signing. Proves the signature covers the transaction body, which is the property the whole scheme exists for.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: the destination array is inside the signed range

vectors.note: the three option-byte accessors read with mutually distinct non-zero sentinels. Every transaction above has options[0] == options[1] == 0x00, because TXDAT_MDST and TXDSA_WOTS are both 0x00, so across all of them TXDAT_TYPE, TXDSA_TYPE and a function returning a constant zero produce identical results.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: TXDAT_TYPE, TXDSA_TYPE and MDST_COUNT are three different reads -- options[0], options[1] and options[2] + 1

vectors.note: the same four sentinels rotated one position. Distinguishes each accessor from a constant return: the correct answer moves.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: TXDAT_TYPE, TXDSA_TYPE and MDST_COUNT are three different reads -- options[0], options[1] and options[2] + 1

vectors.note: rotated once more, so each accessor takes a third distinct value.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: TXDAT_TYPE, TXDSA_TYPE and MDST_COUNT are three different reads -- options[0], options[1] and options[2] + 1

vectors.note: NEGATIVE -- an unrecognised TXDAT_TYPE. Nothing above reaches either rejection arm, because every transaction in the group carries the one recognised value.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: tx__init rejects an unknown TXDAT_TYPE and writes nothing before doing so

vectors.note: NEGATIVE -- a recognised TXDAT_TYPE and an unrecognised TXDSA_TYPE, so the first switch passes and dsaoff is computed before the second rejects.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: tx__init rejects an unknown TXDSA_TYPE and writes nothing before doing so

vectors.note: four destinations, each carrying a DISTINCT non-zero reference the validator accepts. Until this vector the whole group carried exactly one ref value across every destination of every wire image, and it was all zero -- so a serializer that ignored the field reproduced all 43 byte for byte. D10 pins the grammar on a bare 16-byte buffer; this pins the field inside a transaction, at its offset, in bytes the reference laid out. Errata 134.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: MDST is tag(20) then ref(16) then amount(8), and the ref travels in the transaction rather than beside it

vectors.note: NEGATIVE, and the reason D16 means anything: destination 0 carries a reference the validator accepts and destination 1 carries one it rejects. Without this, D16's VEOK is equally the answer a validator that never looked at the field would give. mdst_val reaches the ref check last, after sort, amount, self-send and both add64s, so destination 0 passed all of those before destination 1 failed here.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: mdst_val runs the ref grammar over each destination and rejects the transaction with EMCM_XTXREF
vectors.mdst_val_errno_text: Invalid reference format in eXtended Transaction

vectors.note: the change address carries the SOURCE tag half and the change identity's hash half, so its two halves differ. Every other wire image in the group has chg.tag == chg.hash, because addr_from_wots runs every address through addr_from_implicit, which writes the same 20 bytes into both. THE SERIALIZER-FACING PROPERTY: this is the first image where tag_ptr and hash_ptr select different bytes, so a wrong ADDR_HASH_OFF flips a recorded boolean -- on every existing image both predicates hold under any offset, which is precisely why nothing caught it (errata 124). Ds8b did this for src_addr and nothing had done it for chg_addr. The C-facing property is separate and weaker: the two booleans below are what tx_val requires, but tx_val was NEVER CALLED -- see rule_not_evaluated. This is an image two comparators approve of, not one a validator accepted end to end.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: an address is tag(20) then hash(20) and the two halves are independent; tx_val requires the change address to share the source's tag and differ in its hash

vectors.note: the four 64-bit header fields carrying four MUTUALLY DISTINCT asymmetric values. D8 pins byte order and only partly: it gave send_total, fee_total and blk_to_live the same value, so a serializer writing those three in the wrong order passes it, and it left change_total all-0xff -- a palindrome, in the vector whose own note explains why a palindrome is insufficient. Four distinct values catch field-swap as well as byte order. Each field records its VALUE beside its bytes, because decoding the bytes little-endian and comparing to the value is what tests the order; comparing bytes alone is not. Errata 134.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: send_total, change_total, fee_total and blk_to_live are four separate little-endian 64-bit fields at four fixed offsets

vectors.note: NEGATIVE -- send_total is one greater than the sum of the destination amounts. mdst_val tallies the array with the reference's own add64 and compares, so a builder whose header total disagrees with the destinations it wrote is rejected here. The difference is one unit deliberately: an obviously wrong total would not distinguish a tally that is absent from one that is off.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: send_total must equal the sum of the destination amounts, checked by mdst_val
vectors.mdst_val_errno_text: eXtended TX total does not match tally

vectors.note: NEGATIVE -- fee_total is one below the minimum, which mdst_val accumulates as one MFEE per destination rather than one per transaction. A builder that charges a single MFEE for a multi-destination transaction is rejected here, and the whole corpus had no vector for it.
vectors.falsifies: survey §4: the minimum fee scales with the destination count -- mdst_val adds MFEE once per destination
vectors.mdst_val_errno_text: eXtended TX fee does not match tally
